description: Exact-match rows for schema tickets, customers, assets, timers, system, settings, events, users, api_keys, trace, errors or counters only. Timers are read here (there is no get_timer): state, elapsed_ms and remaining_ms are worked out when you query. system is one row about this machine: memory, CPU, disk and whether it is in a container (inside Docker those are the container limits); there is no system_info tool. settings is one row: the saved settings, with no API keys or passwords (there is no get_settings tool); change them with update_settings (MQTT: set_mqtt). events are the events already announced, newest first; filter type takes a name or a group such as ticket.*. users and api_keys need an admin credential and never contain a password or a key secret; there is no list_users or list_api_keys tool. trace (the call trace, only while audit is on), errors (failed calls) and counters (success, error and denied per tool) also need an admin credential; there is no export_log tool. tickets: this is how tickets are found and read (there is no search_tickets or get_ticket tool). filter status (open, pending, solved), requester_email, attribution, query (a keyword in subject or body), or id for one ticket with its body and comments. A list returns the short fields; pass fields to choose others. customers: filter email for one customer (there is no lookup_customer tool). phone is the text REDACTED unless you present a credential with the pii scope. Do not pass a tool name or a singular data name. Do not invent query_tickets or query_with_filter. Empty rows mean no match; loosen the filter, do not retry the same query.

fields.description: Optional field projection. Example: ["id","subject"]. Omit for the default fields; a tickets id filter returns every field.

filter.description: Optional map. Keys must be listed in get_schema.filterable. Exact match, except tickets query, which is a keyword. Examples: {"status":"open"}, {"id":"TCK-1001"}, {"query":"password"}.

limit.description: Max rows to return. Default 10, max 50.

schema.description: tickets, customers, assets, timers, system, settings, events, users, api_keys, trace, errors or counters only. Not ticket, customer, server, and not a tool name such as describe_server.

name: run_query
